scope: Read-only source review of five RTL modules against D0-D2 release/contracts; no regression rerun and no implementation changes

findings.title: Final output can assert success before an accepted old-task illegal command retires
findings.trigger: At DRAIN on the final matrix record, use out_ready=1, old q_valid=0 and in_valid=1 with in_op=7 and in_task_id equal to the active task. The command is accepted on the same edge as final out_fire.
findings.reasoning: in_ready algebraically equals !fault because retire_event=q_valid&&!fault. On that final edge the command only enters q_*, so retire_event is false and the normal DRAIN branch asserts core_done and IDLE. The newly accepted invalid command retires on the following edge and sets fault, after a success pulse was already visible. The queue is not empty when success is generated.
findings.consequence: A consumer may commit success for a task that already accepted an invalid event and faults immediately afterward, contrary to the release requirement that internal entries be empty and no task fault precede core_done.
findings.evidence_type: cycle-accurate static reasoning; directed simulation pending root reproduction
findings.existing_test_gap: d2_protocol.py fault_on_fire injects on an early published 64-word block, not on the final matrix record with the entry queue initially empty.
findings.requested_validation: Add a directed public-port test for illegal event accepted exactly on final out_fire (also final-1 and final+1 boundaries), verify no successful done for the failed task, preserve published payload during stalls, and rerun affected acceptance after a fix.

checked_paths.result: No in-scope arithmetic issue found. signed49 add, signed48 clipping, magnitude-based symmetric ties-to-even and signed32 clipping are correctly separated for shift0..47.
No last-product loss found. cfg clears lanes, 64 issued values retire before FINAL_SUM and quantization; sparse active masks and stalled output ownership remain stable.

X and W bank/address formulas correspond to the declared m*64+k and k*16+j layout; counters advance on actual ordered retire and START cannot bypass the final parameter write in the current one-entry design.
LAT1/LAT2 valid pipelines are consumed with one vector outstanding; effective row mask prevents unused tail reads, and accumulation uses a registered signed product before quantization.

Normal output payload and last stay stable until handshake. Existing fault logic preserves and drains a published block without done when the fault is already known; the newly accepted final-edge command gap is the finding above.

checked_paths.path: reset blocks in all five modules
checked_paths.result: Synchronous active-low reset clears valid/control/tag/count state and does not clear bulk RAM. Subsequent complete cold load prevents stale X/W/B reads.

assumptions_and_boundaries: core supported geometry is K64, PN4, N_TILE16, M1..99, N16..256 multiple16, PM1/2/4, READ_LATENCY1/2; standalone micro parameters are not generally validated.
quant_epilogue and micro_tile assume shift0..47; core BEGIN explicitly validates it.

banked_sp16 assumes no simultaneous write/read on a single bank; integrated core guarantees mutual exclusion through LOAD vs READ state. Its standalone rd_valid would otherwise claim a read while write wins.
No claim of synthesis, SRAM macro mapping, 150MHz, area, power, E203 integration, official600 or formal12 performance acceptance.
This is an independent source review, not independent execution of the 36-case regression; parent acceptance must separately verify current source and evidence identities.
